verifications.verifierNote: Pattern present. src/test/setup.ts is 14 lines (jest-dom, fake-indexeddb, configure({asyncUtilTimeout:5000}) at line 9, afterEach cleanup at 11-14) with no fetch helper. All four stubs verified: smoke.test.tsx:43, covers/index.test.ts:8, :56 (zero-param throwing stub), :64. vite.config.ts:24 sets restoreMocks:true with no unstubGlobals, and smoke.test.tsx:61 does call vi.unstubAllGlobals() as the last statement of the test BODY while covers/index.test.ts:16-18 uses afterEach — the asymmetry is real. Two claims overstate: (a) a one-parameter function IS legally assignable to typeof fetch in TS, so 'drops init' is not a type error and no production init is 'silently discarded' any differently than by a stub that ignores it; (b) the category unknown-misuse points at vitest's own vi.stubGlobal(name, value: unknown) signature, which is third-party, not source — the spec excludes library-side types from per-file findings. What survives is genuine but test-only: nothing checks the stubs against typeof globalThis.fetch, and the leak risk at smoke.test.tsx:61 is real test hygiene rather than a type weakness. Spec reserves low for exactly this ('any in test fixtures ... worth fixing for hygiene but won't cause incidents').
verifications.reachability: Test-only. If any assertion between smoke.test.tsx:49-60 throws, line 61 never runs and the 200-'{}' stub leaks into the two later tests in the file (lines 64 and 85), which would then exercise a stubbed network. No production path is affected.
verifications.blastRadius: 4 stub sites in 2 test files; 0 production files.
verifications.suggestedPatch: In src/test/setup.ts add `export function stubFetch(impl: typeof globalThis.fetch) { vi.stubGlobal('fetch', vi.fn(impl)); }` and extend the existing afterEach (line 11) with `vi.unstubAllGlobals();`. Replace the four hand-rolled stubs with stubFetch(...) and delete smoke.test.tsx:61 plus covers/index.test.ts:16-18. Risk: the global unstub in afterEach would also clear a stub a test intended to outlive it — no test does that today.
verifications.amendedDescription: src/test/setup.ts provides no shared, typed fetch stub, so four hand-rolled stubs (smoke.test.tsx:43; covers/index.test.ts:8, :56, :64) are each written against an ad-hoc signature that nothing checks against `typeof globalThis.fetch`. The practical consequence is not the omitted `init` parameter (legal in TS) but that `mock.calls` entries are typed to whatever the stub declared, so an assertion over the request options is untypeable, and that cleanup is per-file convention: smoke.test.tsx:61 unstubs inside the test body, so a failing assertion at lines 49-60 leaks a blanket 200 stub into the rest of the file. Test-hygiene severity; no production path is affected.

verifications.verifierNote: Pattern present exactly as described: smoke.test.tsx:58-60 is `for (const call of fetchSpy.mock.calls) { expect(String(call[0])).not.toContain('generativelanguage'); }` with no expect.assertions and no toHaveBeenCalled, so on the intended-pass path (zero captured calls) the assertion body never executes. That is a genuinely vacuous test guarding a stated CLAUDE.md invariant. However this is a test-assertion-strength defect, not a type weakness: nothing here is typed via assertion and no external data enters typed code, so the assigned category boundary-without-validation does not hold. The only type-adjacent residue is that the stub at line 43 declares one parameter, so `call` is a 1-tuple and `String(call[0])` is the only expressible assertion (see F101). Discovery's alternative (b) — a fetch reference captured at module-import time before the stub at line 47 — is not supported: the Gemini client is resolved lazily via getClient() at call time, not at import.
verifications.reachability: The vacuous branch is the normal green path — the test passes today having asserted nothing. A future refactor that moves the Gemini call outside the spy's reach would also pass silently.
verifications.blastRadius: 1 test; the same vacuous-loop shape is repeated at covers/index.test.ts:72-74.
verifications.suggestedPatch: Replace smoke.test.tsx:58-60 with `const geminiCalls = fetchSpy.mock.calls.filter(([input]) => String(input).includes('generativelanguage')); expect(geminiCalls).toEqual([]);` and move vi.unstubAllGlobals() out of the body into an afterEach. verifications.amendedDescription: smoke.test.tsx:58-60 asserts the 'no Gemini call on boot' invariant with a for-loop over fetchSpy.mock.calls that runs zero times on the intended-pass path, so the test passes having asserted nothing. verifications.verifierNote: Every cited site verified. types.ts:24 `createdAt: string`, :39 `addedAt`, :40 `finishedAt?`, :62 `generatedAt`, :93 `dueAt` — all bare strings. The lexicographic dependence is real and load-bearing: repo.ts:9 `all.sort((a,b) => a.createdAt.localeCompare(b.createdAt))` and repo.ts:87-89 `.filter(card => card.dueAt <= cutoff).sort((a,b) => a.dueAt.localeCompare(b.dueAt))`, with the assumption written out in the comment at repo.ts:83. The live ingress is confirmed: migrate.ts:95 passes `legacyProfile?.joinedAt` — an arbitrary JSON value obtained through the `JSON.parse(raw) as T` assertion at migrate.ts:54-62 — into profiles.create, and repo.ts:24 stores it verbatim (`input.createdAt ?? new Date().toISOString()`; note `??` rescues null/undefined but not a number or an object). A stored number then makes repo.ts:9 throw 'a.createdAt.localeCompare is not a function' on every profile-list load, durably, and ProfileView.tsx:54 `new Date(profile.createdAt)` renders 'Invalid Date'. Amending the category: the defect that can actually bite is the unvalidated localStorage ingress at one line, not the absence of branding across five fields — branding is the fix shape, not the finding.
verifications.reachability: Legacy user with `booksum_profile_<id>` in localStorage whose joinedAt is not a string (hand-edited, or written by an older build as a Date/number). migrateLegacyData runs once on boot (migrate.ts:80-96) -> profiles.create -> IndexedDB. Thereafter profiles.list() throws on every load and the profile picker cannot render.
verifications.blastRadius: createdAt is read at repo.ts:9 and ProfileView.tsx:54; the same ISO-sorts-chronologically assumption also carries repo.ts:88-89 for dueAt (which has no external ingress — see F112). One unvalidated producer: migrate.ts:95.
verifications.suggestedPatch: At migrate.ts:95: `createdAt: typeof legacyProfile?.joinedAt === 'string' && !Number.isNaN(Date.parse(legacyProfile.joinedAt)) ? legacyProfile.joinedAt : undefined` — repo.ts:24's `?? new Date().toISOString()` then supplies the fallback. Risk: none; a non-ISO legacy joinedAt is replaced by migration time rather than being persisted. verifications.amendedDescription: ISO-8601 timestamps across Profile/Book/Summary/ReviewCard are bare strings whose lexicographic ordering is load-bearing (repo.ts:9, repo.ts:88-89), and one of them is fed unvalidated from localStorage: migrate.ts:95 pipes legacyProfile?.joinedAt (obtained through the `JSON.parse as T` assertion at migrate.ts:54-62) into profiles.create, which stores it verbatim at repo.ts:24. verifications.verifierNote: Both halves of the pattern verified. types.ts:6-15 declares the eight-member `Category` enum and types.ts:33 declares `category: string`; a repo-wide grep for the identifier returns only its own declaration at types.ts:6 — every other hit is JSX label text (BookDetail.tsx:321, StatsView.tsx:133/138) or an `activeCategory` local (LibraryPage.tsx:22/47/110/174-177). The enum is dead. Producers confirmed: summarize.ts:26 `category: data.category || 'Other'` where data is the raw JSON.parse cast at summarize.ts:52/73, schemas.ts:8 `category: { type: Type.STRING }` with no enum constraint, useLibrary.tsx:154 and migrate.ts:109. What breaks Discovery's severity is the consumer: LibraryPage.tsx:65 builds the chip list as `['All', ...Array.from(new Set(books.map((b) => b.category)))]` — derived from the books themselves — so the exact-match filter at LibraryPage.tsx:47 always has a matching chip and no book is ever unreachable. The real consequence is fragmentation ('Self-Help' vs 'Self Help' become two chips and two rows in the StatsView breakdown at StatsView.tsx:23-28), which is cosmetic. verifications.blastRadius: One dead enum; four producers (summarize.ts:26, useLibrary.tsx:154, migrate.ts:109, plus the raw model value); three consumers (LibraryPage.tsx:47/65, StatsView.tsx:23-28, markdown.ts:13).

'') ? data.category! : 'Other'`), leaving Book.category as `string` so already-stored free-form values still load. AddBookModal.tsx:76/78 does derive both from the same `pdf` local, so the two agree there by convention (note line 76 also overrides the hasPdf that summarize.ts:31 already put on generated.book — the same fact is stated three times on one path). After any backup restore, every PDF book has hasPdf true with no blob row; BookDetail.tsx:196-198 renders the Open-PDF affordance, `blobs.get` returns undefined, and handleOpenPdf returns silently at line 198. verifications.verifierNote: Confirmed end to end and promoted. types.ts:88-89 places `options: string[]` and `correctAnswerIndex: number` side by side with no expressed relation. The value's origin is Gemini: schemas.ts:69-72 constrains it only with the natural-language description 'Index (0-3) of the correct answer in the options array' (and options only with 'Array of 4 possible answers.'), and quiz.ts:16 takes it off a raw `JSON.parse(response.text || '{}') as { questions?: QuizQuestion[] }` cast. QuizModal.tsx:50-61 then feeds each question straight into srs.ts:22-35 newCard, which copies correctAnswerIndex verbatim at srs.ts:29, and QuizModal.tsx:52 persists the card with reviewCards.upsert. There is no bounds check on any of those five hops. Consumers compare for equality: ReviewPage.tsx:76 `selected === current.correctAnswerIndex` and :94 `index === current.correctAnswerIndex`, plus QuizModal.tsx:78. This satisfies the spec's High bar on two counts — a known-runtime-data ingress with no validation, and durability: the bad index is written to IndexedDB, and because a wrong answer grades 1, scheduleCard (srs.ts:45-46) resets intervalDays to 1, so the unanswerable card returns every single day, permanently.
verifications.reachability: Take a quiz on any book with a Gemini key. A model that returns 1-based indices (a classic structured-output failure the schema's prose description does not prevent) yields correctAnswerIndex 4 on a 4-element options array: every option renders un-highlighted, ReviewPage.tsx:76 is false for every choice, the card can never be answered correctly, and it resurfaces daily forever. Only deleting the book (books.remove -> reviewCards.removeByBook, repo.ts:72) clears it.
verifications.blastRadius: One ingress (quiz.ts:16) feeding one writer (QuizModal.tsx:52-61 via srs.ts:29) and three consumer sites (ReviewPage.tsx:76, ReviewPage.tsx:94, QuizModal.tsx:78). Every review card in the database originates here.
verifications.suggestedPatch: In quiz.ts, replace `return data.questions ?? []` (line 17) with a validating filter: `return (data.questions ?? []).filter((q) => Array.isArray(q.options) && q.options.length > 0 && Number.isInteger(q.correctAnswerIndex) && q.correctAnswerIndex >= 0 && q.correctAnswerIndex < q.options.length)`. Risk: a model returning 1-based indices now produces an empty quiz instead of a broken one, so QuizModal should surface a toast when the filtered list is empty rather than rendering a zero-question quiz.
verifications.amendedDescription: ReviewCard.correctAnswerIndex (types.ts:89) has no type-level relation to ReviewCard.options (types.ts:88), and the value arrives unvalidated from Gemini — schemas.ts:69-72 expresses the 0-3 range only as prose, quiz.ts:16 casts JSON.parse output straight to QuizQuestion[], srs.ts:29 copies it verbatim, and QuizModal.tsx:52 persists the card to IndexedDB. An out-of-range index makes the card permanently unanswerable at ReviewPage.tsx:76/94, and because a wrong answer grades 1 the SM-2 scheduler (srs.ts:45-46) resets the interval to one day, so the corrupt card resurfaces every day until the book is deleted. Unvalidated AI ingress plus durable persistence puts this at high.

verifications.verifierNote: Verified in full. types.ts:99 `version: 2` is a literal, so within the program every LibraryExport is definitionally v2; useLibrary.tsx:94 is the only producer. On the read side ProfileView.tsx:116-117 does `const content = e.target?.result as string; const data = JSON.parse(content) as LibraryExport;` and the sole check is `if (!Array.isArray(data.books))` at line 119 — nothing reads data.version. importLibrary (useLibrary.tsx:102-122) likewise never mentions payload.version; it iterates payload.books and calls bookRepo.create with `{...book, profileId}` (line 111) and upserts payload.summaries verbatim (line 115). So the one field designed as a schema discriminant is load-bearing for nothing, and arbitrary user-supplied JSON reaches IndexedDB after a single Array.isArray check. Recategorising: the operative defect is the unvalidated file boundary, not a missing tag union — the tag exists and is simply unread. Severity medium holds: the app is local-first with no accounts, the user picks their own file, and the damage is garbage rows rather than compromise.
verifications.reachability: Profile -> Import backup -> any JSON file with a `books` array passes ProfileView.tsx:119 and every element is written to IndexedDB. A v1 backup (implied by the `version: 2` literal) imports as v2 with no warning; a hand-edited or truncated file imports its rows verbatim, and useLibrary.tsx:114 `for (const summary of payload.summaries ?? [])` throws TypeError on a non-iterable summaries value.
verifications.blastRadius: One writer (useLibrary.tsx:94), one reader (ProfileView.tsx:117 -> useLibrary.tsx:102-122); every book and summary row a restore creates.
verifications.suggestedPatch: At ProfileView.tsx:117 parse to a wider type first — `const data = JSON.parse(content) as Partial<LibraryExport> & { version?: number }` — then reject early: `if (data.version !== 2 || !Array.isArray(data.books) || !Array.isArray(data.summaries)) { toast.error('That is not a BookSum backup file.'); setImportStatus('error'); return; }`. Risk: files produced before the version field existed would now be rejected — acceptable, and better than silently merging an unknown shape.
verifications.amendedDescription: LibraryExport.version (types.ts:99) is a literal-typed discriminant that no consumer reads: ProfileView.tsx:117 asserts an arbitrary parsed file straight into the interface and checks only `Array.isArray(data.books)` (line 119), and importLibrary (useLibrary.tsx:102-122) never inspects payload.version before writing every row into IndexedDB via bookRepo.create (line 111) and summaryRepo.upsert (line 115). The defect is an unvalidated file boundary rather than a missing union — the tag is present and unused.

verifications.verifierNote: Re-measured: `npx tsc --noEmit --noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature` emits exactly 5 errors, all TS4111 at googleBooks.ts 19, 20, 21, 22, 23 — matching the claim precisely. The substance behind the flag is the real finding and it holds: googleBooks.ts:12-14 casts `await response.json()` to `{ items?: { volumeInfo?: { imageLinks?: Record<string, string> } }[] }`, and `Record<string, string>` asserts total key coverage, so when `links` is defined the compiler believes `links.extraLarge` is a `string` and treats the whole `?? links?.large ?? ... ?? links?.smallThumbnail` tail at lines 19-23 as unreachable. The Google Books API in fact commonly returns only smallThumbnail and thumbnail, so the declared type is false at an external-API boundary — the textbook lying type. No live defect: the `??` chain and the `if (url)` guard at line 24 handle the undefined the type denies, and a miss falls through to OpenLibrary and then the local placeholder. Medium is right for a boundary type that is wrong but currently harmless.
verifications.reachability: Every cover lookup hits it, so the wrong type is exercised on essentially every request; only the defensive `??` chain keeps it from mattering.
verifications.blastRadius: One file, one boundary; fetchGoogleBooksCover has a single consumer in src/lib/covers/index.ts.
verifications.suggestedPatch: Replace the cast at googleBooks.ts:13 with `imageLinks?: Partial<Record<'extraLarge' | 'large' | 'medium' | 'thumbnail' | 'smallThumbnail', string>>`. The `??` chain then type-checks as genuinely fallible and the 5 TS4111 errors disappear without enabling the flag. Risk: none — no runtime change, and it documents the API's real optionality.

verifications.verifierNote: Pattern present: repo.ts:78-81 listByProfile does `getAll('reviewCards')` then reads `card.profileId`, repo.ts:94-97 listByBook does the same for bookId, and listDue at repo.ts:84-90 filters on `card.dueAt <= cutoff` (line 88) and sorts with `a.dueAt.localeCompare(b.dueAt)` (line 89) on rows typed only by the declaration at db.ts:12-16. Two of Discovery's claims do not survive. First, there is no ingress: the only writers to the reviewCards store are QuizModal.tsx:52 and useReviewQueue.ts:38, both routed through srs.ts, and both newCard (srs.ts:33) and scheduleCard (srs.ts:52) set dueAt from `new Date(...).toISOString()`. Neither the legacy migration nor the backup import touches reviewCards — so unlike summaries (F113) or profiles (F103) no non-string dueAt can arrive without direct database tampering. The full-table-scan vs by-profile-due-index point is a performance observation, which the spec places out of scope. Downgrading to low.

verifications.verifierNote: Verified. repo.ts:129-139 blobs.put writes `type: blob.type` verbatim at line 138 and blobs.get replays it into `new Blob([record.bytes], { type: record.type })` at line 144, while types.ts:71/79 declare `kind: BlobKind` and `type: string` with no relationship — a 'pdf' record may legitimately carry any MIME string. The write source is confirmed as a user-picked File: AddBookModal.tsx:35 holds `File | null`, the accept='.pdf' attribute is a dialog hint only, and useLibrary.tsx:51 forwards it. The consumer chain is as described: BookDetail.tsx:197-200 gets the blob, `URL.createObjectURL(pdf)` (199) and `window.open(url, '_blank')` (200). The security reasoning is technically correct — a blob: URL inherits the creating document's origin, so a stored text/html type means script executing in the app's origin, where the Gemini key lives in localStorage. One reachability gate Discovery omits, which is why I am not promoting this to high: AddBookModal.tsx:59-67 only assigns `pdf = file` (line 66) after `summarizePdf(base64)` (line 65) resolves, so a non-PDF must first be accepted by Gemini as inlineData mimeType application/pdf; and a file merely renamed to .pdf is typed application/pdf by the browser and renders as a PDF, not as HTML.

verifications.verifierNote: Verified: types.ts:79 declares `type: string`, repo.ts:138 stores whatever `blob.type` the browser derived from the picked File, repo.ts:144 replays it into the reconstructed Blob, and BookDetail.tsx:195-200 hands the resulting object URL to window.open. BlobKind is a proper literal union (types.ts:4) and is used correctly at the call site (`blobs.get(book.id, 'pdf')`, line 197) but is not connected to the MIME string, so the two can disagree with nothing to catch it. The `''` scenario is the plausible one: browsers derive File.type from the extension and normally yield application/pdf for .pdf, but an OS without the mapping registered yields '', after which window.open shows a blank tab or a download instead of a rendered PDF — a button that looks broken with no error surfaced. Note the migration path is safe because migrate.ts:137/143 hardcodes the MIME types. This is the consumer-side view of F114 and shares one fix; keeping it at low since the consequence here is UX rather than the origin concern.
